films.title: Persona
films.lead: An actress stops speaking. A nurse talks enough for both of them.
films.note: Bergman presses two faces together until they blur. The screen burns through once, near the start, and the film never quite puts itself back. Eighty-three minutes with nothing spare in them.

films.title: El Sur
films.lead: A daughter grows up in the north of Spain, watching her father for clues.
films.note: Erice made this for television and it was cut before release, so what survives is unfinished on purpose. A girl, a house, a father who keeps one door closed. The last scene arrives like a held breath.

films.title: C'mon C'mon
films.lead: A radio journalist takes his nephew on a road trip and interviews children about the future.
films.note: Mostly filmed in cars and hotel rooms, in black and white. The interviews are real children and they carry the film. A movie about listening that actually listens.

films.title: First Cow
films.lead: Two outsiders steal milk from the only cow in Oregon to sell fried dough.
films.note: A frontier film with no heroism in it, only labour and friendship. Reichardt keeps the camera low and patient. The last ten minutes are as tense as any thriller.

films.title: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On
films.lead: A one-inch shell with one eye searches for his family inside an Airbnb.
films.note: Stop-motion pretending to be a documentary. Funny for ten minutes, then quietly devastating about being the one who got left behind.

films.title: The Florida Project
films.lead: Children run wild through a motel outside Walt Disney World.
films.note: Baker shoots on 35mm in colours that do not belong to these lives. Moonee's summer is a game for as long as it can stay one. The final shot changes format and it hurts.

films.title: Hereditary
films.lead: A family loses its grandmother and inherits something worse.
films.note: Aster builds his horror out of miniature models, homework and silence before he lets it go loud. The last act takes everything. It earns it.

films.title: Showing Up
films.lead: A sculptor in Portland tries to finish work for a show while everybody interrupts her.
films.note: The least dramatic film on this list. A cat, a kiln, a broken water heater, a brother who is not well. Reichardt argues that making things is mostly errands.

films.title: The Banshees of Inisherin
films.lead: One friend stops speaking to the other, on an island where nothing else happens.
films.note: Played straight and photographed beautifully. The civil war across the water is the hum underneath. McDonagh's funniest film and his bleakest, which is saying something.

films.title: The Substance
films.lead: A fading star injects a black-market serum and is issued a younger version of herself.
films.note: Fargeat shoots close, wet and very loud. Body horror aimed at anyone who has been told to keep producing. The audience noise is part of the show.

films.title: Misericordia
films.lead: A man returns to his village for a funeral and then stays too long.
films.note: Guiraudie's people have no shame and no plan. A death, a priest, a night walk in the woods, all delivered in the flattest possible tone.

films.title: The Lovers
films.lead: A married couple, both having affairs, fall back in love with each other.
films.note: Debra Winger and Tracy Letts are the entire engine. A comedy about cheating that refuses to judge anybody in it.

films.title: Talk to Me
films.lead: Teenagers get hold of a hand that lets the dead speak through them.
films.note: Made by the RackaRacka brothers, so it moves fast and does not flinch. Grief, peer pressure and possession inside ninety-four minutes.

films.title: Civil War
films.lead: A photo team drives to Washington through a country at war with itself.
films.note: Garland keeps the politics vague on purpose and stays with the journalists. A war film about the habit of looking, with one very quiet scene in a house that stops the film cold.

films.title: Aftersun
films.lead: A young father and his daughter on a package holiday, remembered years later.
films.note: Wells films it twice at once, what happened and what a daughter can now see in it. Almost nothing is said out loud.

films.title: Paris, Texas
films.lead: A man walks out of the desert and slowly accounts for his life.
films.note: Wenders and Ry Cooder make the American west feel empty and loud at the same time. The last scene in the booth is a whole film on its own.

films.title: Cléo from 5 to 7
films.lead: Ninety minutes in the life of a singer waiting on a medical result.
films.note: Varda keeps it in real time and mostly on the street. The fear loosens exactly when Cléo stops looking at herself.

films.title: The Zone of Interest
films.lead: The commandant of Auschwitz and his wife build a garden against the camp wall.
films.note: All of it is in the sound. The camera never crosses the wall and you never stop hearing what is behind it.

films.title: Moonlight
films.lead: Three chapters in the life of a boy in Miami who cannot say what he wants.
films.note: Jenkins shoots in blue and skin, and hands the last chapter to a man who has learned to perform all of it.

films.title: The Lighthouse
films.lead: Two men, one rock, a lamp neither of them is allowed to touch.
films.note: Black and white, boxed into an almost square frame, wet and loud. A duel about work, drink and the light upstairs.
